---
name: Marie
surname: Curie
position: "Physicist and Chemist"
address: "Paris, France"
email: "marie.curie@example.org"
github: mcurie
# Every design places a profile picture; a square image crops best. Each sets
# its own width, and `profilepic-width` overrides it.
# profilepic: "profile.jpg"
# Uncomment to add more to the header:
# phone: "+33 1 23 45 67 89"
# www: "example.org"
# orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000
# linkedin: mcurie
# profilepic-width: "0.25\\linewidth"
# footer: "A trailing line, set in the accent colour."
# The accent colour every design builds its headings from. `headcolor` is
# accepted as an alias, so the same front matter drives the other quarto-vitae
# templates.
# sectcol: "0096FF"
# Each design is its own extension, so switching is a one-line change:
#   latexcv-classic-pdf       latexcv-rows-pdf
#   latexcv-modern-pdf        latexcv-sidebar-pdf
#   latexcv-minimalistic-pdf  latexcv-sidebarleft-pdf
#   latexcv-twocolumn-pdf
format: latexcv-classic-pdf
# The sidebar designs fill their column from here. Every other design ignores
# it, so it can stay in the document as you switch between them.
sidebar:
  - title: Techniques
    items:
      - Fractional crystallisation
      - Quartz electrometry
      - Radiometric measurement
  - title: Fields
    items:
      # `stars` and `bar` work here as they do in the body, and are
      # interchangeable. This column sets a rating on the line below what it
      # rates, so no break is written for either.
      - "Radioactivity {{< stars 5 >}}"
      - "Spectroscopy {{< bar 60% >}}"
  - title: Languages
    items:
      - Polish, French, Russian
---

# Education

Each row is one entry, each column a field. `fields` renames a column the style
does not expect, like `dplyr::rename()`.

::: {.entries style="detailed" fields="{what: Degree, with: Institution, when: Years, where: Location}"}
| Degree             | Institution         | Years     | Location      |
|--------------------|---------------------|-----------|---------------|
| Ph.D. in Physics   | University of Paris | 1891-1895 | Paris, France |
| M.Sc. in Chemistry | University of Paris | 1889-1891 | Paris, France |
:::

# Employment

A grid table can hold a bullet list in a cell, so `why` carries several points
per entry. Here the headings already match, and no `fields` is needed.

::: {.entries style="detailed"}
+------------+---------------------+-----------+------------------------------+
| what       | with                | when      | why                          |
+============+=====================+===========+==============================+
| Professor  | University of Paris | 1906-1934 | - First woman to hold the    |
|            |                     |           |   chair of General Physics   |
|            |                     |           | - Directed the Curie         |
|            |                     |           |   Laboratory                 |
+------------+---------------------+-----------+------------------------------+
| Researcher | EPCI                | 1897-1906 | - Isolated polonium and      |
|            |                     |           |   radium                     |
+------------+---------------------+-----------+------------------------------+
:::

# Awards

The `brief` style is a single line per entry, for lists needing no elaboration.

::: {.entries style="brief"}
| what                     | where           | when |
|--------------------------|-----------------|------|
| Nobel Prize in Chemistry | Swedish Academy | 1911 |
| Davy Medal               | Royal Society   | 1903 |
| Nobel Prize in Physics   | Swedish Academy | 1903 |
:::

# Service

Markdown inside cells is preserved and LaTeX special characters are escaped, so
*emphasis* and a literal 100% both come out right.

::: {.entries style="brief"}
| what                                 | where    | when |
|--------------------------------------|----------|------|
| Member, *Solvay Council*             | Brussels | 1911 |
| Director, Red Cross Radiology (100%) | Paris    | 1914 |
:::

# Skills

The `skills` style pairs a category with its members. A rating is content, not a
field: `{{{< stars 4 >}}}` and `{{{< bar 80% >}}}` work in any cell.

::: {.entries style="skills"}
| what            | with                                             |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Radiochemistry  | {{< bar 100% >}}                                 |
| Electrometry    | {{< stars 8/10 >}} piezoelectric quartz          |
| Languages       | Polish, French, Russian                          |
:::
